subject: journey/odyssey
prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: a single landscape 3:2 page from the Odyssey sketchbook. An illustrated page from an explorer's journal: one particular moment on the journey, drawn close enough to see faces, hands, tools, clothing and the things being traded, measured or found. The traveller need not appear: some pages record only what the party saw (a harbour, a fortress, a market, an animal or plant). When the traveller does appear, draw them in action and in a natural, varied pose, not standing to attention. In the manner of the expedition artists of the 18th and 19th centuries. A visible graphite underdrawing with construction lines left in; quick sepia and brown ink with loose hatching; watercolour dropped in quickly and unevenly in a few washes of ochre, grey-green, faded blue and a touch of red. The page may carry one or two small separate studies of a detail (an object, a tool, a creature) loosely arranged beside the main scene, as on a real sketchbook page. Edges unfinished, dissolving into bare, slightly foxed cream paper; a single page, no binding visible. No legible writing of any kind: no annotations, labels, captions, numbers, dates or signature; any writing that appears in the scene is illegible marks. No border or frame. Nothing anachronistic for the year given; people, dress and objects true to their place and time, drawn with respect.

This page contains no recognisable major character. Imagined episode from Homer’s Odyssey, with a plausible late Bronze Age material setting. A view recorded by the fleeing crew, with none of the travelling party visible: a narrow enclosed harbour seen from the open sea, towering cliffs, giant silhouettes above hurling rocks, small shattered wooden ships trapped inside. Emphasise the shape of the enclosing harbour and the vast difference in scale. No Odysseus, no close-up human portrait, no gore. No modern objects, later triremes or medieval architecture.
